Australia jobs preview: NAB sees 20,000 gain, unemployment steady at 4.6%
articles.desc: With NAB, Westpac and consensus all at 20,000 and three major banks seeing unemployment at 4.6%, the bar for a surprise sits mainly in the jobless rate. A drop to 4.5% would revive the case for further RBA tightening and could support the Australian dollar and short-dated yields. A rise to 4.7% woul
articles.content: With NAB, Westpac and consensus all at 20,000 and three major banks seeing unemployment at 4.6%, the bar for a surprise sits mainly in the jobless rate. A drop to 4.5% would revive the case for further RBA tightening and could support the Australian dollar and short-dated yields. A rise to 4.7% would push the other way, adding weight to the view that four hikes are already doing enough. NAB’s view that the cooling is supply-led also matters for rates: rising labour force participation eases wage pressure without signalling a hiring slump, which gives the RBA less reason to sound alarmed about growth. - NAB thinks August’s jobless jump was partly a statistical quirk, but not enough of one to drag the rate back to 4.5% this month. Summary: Australia’s September labour force data are due at 11.30am Sydney time Thursday (0030 GMT Thursday, 8.30pm US Eastern Wednesday) NAB forecasts employment up 20,000, matching Westpac and consensus, with CBA lower at about 10,000 NAB sees unemployment holding at 4.6%, with some risk of a lower reading That would sit marginally above the RBA’s 4.5% fourth-quarter forecast, which NAB says would not materially change the central bank’s assessment unless unemployment keeps surprising higher NAB said August’s jump looked partly due to residual seasonality and ABS methodology changes, raising the prospect of some payback A low-unemployment survey group rotating out, and rounding, keep NAB from making 4.5% its base case National Australia Bank expects Australia’s September labour force figures to show employment rising by 20,000 and the unemployment rate holding at 4.6%, with some risk of a lower reading. The data are due at 11.30am Sydney time on Thursday, which is 0030 GMT and 8.30pm US Eastern time on Wednesday. NAB’s forecast matches Westpac’s and the market consensus. CBA expects a softer gain of about 10,000. All three banks see unemployment unchanged. A 4.6% reading would leave the jobless rate slightly above the 4.5% fourth-quarter projection in the Reserve Bank of Australia’s August Statement on Monetary Policy, its quarterly economic outlook. NAB does not expect that gap to materially shift the RBA’s view of the labour market unless unemployment keeps surprising higher through to year-end. The bank said much of the recent cooling reflects more people entering the workforce rather than weaker hiring, and that indicators of labour demand remain resilient. NAB said August’s jump in unemployment appeared partly due to residual seasonality and partly due to methodology changes. Residual seasonality refers to seasonal patterns that the adjustment process did not fully strip out. The methodology changes were made under the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ Labour Force Modernisation project. Together, these raise the prospect of some payback this month. Two factors stop NAB from making a 4.5% print its base case. First, the eighth of the survey sample rotating out this month has an unusually low unemployment rate, so its departure tends to push the measured rate higher. Second, August’s rate was about 4.65% before rounding. It could therefore fall almost a full tenth of a percentage point and still be reported as 4.6%. The result feeds directly into the debate over whether the RBA, having lifted its cash rate four times to 4.60%, needs to go further. On NAB’s reading, a steady 4.6% would not be enough to shift that assessment. A run of upside surprises in unemployment through to year-end would be. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Managers Need to Get Better at Killing Digital Products
articles.desc: Companies often hesitate to sunset digital products because they fear customer backlash. But a study of roughly 360 product and service shutdowns over nearly two decades suggests that fear is exaggerated: About two in five generated no measurable public reaction, and only about a third of those that
articles.content: Companies often hesitate to sunset digital products because they fear customer backlash. But a study of roughly 360 product and service shutdowns over nearly two decades suggests that fear is exaggerated: About two in five generated no measurable public reaction, and only about a third of those that were noticed provoked a negative response. The research reveals that companies should separate two questions: Will anyone notice the shutdown, and, if they do, will they be angry? Factors companies can control—including communications—primarily affect visibility, not customer sentiment. Backlash depends more on whom the shutdown leaves behind: Declining products may retain a small but intensely loyal user base particularly prone to protest. Companies should therefore calibrate their shutdown efforts to likely visibility, focus resources on helping highly attached customers transition, and be candid about why a product is ending. Done thoughtfully, sunsetting can free resources for more promising products without creating the reputational damage companies fear.

What Are The Cheapest Bose Headphones You Can Buy In 2026?
articles.desc: Headphones from Bose are usually quite expensive. If you're looking for one that doesn't break the bank, here are the cheapest Bose headphones you can buy.
articles.content: What Are The Cheapest Bose Headphones You Can Buy In 2026? What Are The Cheapest Bose Headphones You Can Buy In 2026? We may receive a commission on purchases made from links. Who doesn't want to own a fantastic pair of headphones? Killer sound quality and features like are staples of over-ear, on-ear, and in-ear audio, and one brand that makes all three is Bose. Unfortunately, Bose cans and buds are some of the more expensive audio products on the market (the same goes for the brand's Bluetooth speakers). Unless you're buying a used or refurbished item, it'll be tough to find Now, 'tough' doesn't translate to 'impossible', and as luck would have it, we actually found a sub-$200 pair of Bose earbuds that can be purchased brand-new. We're talking about the , which hit the market in 2024. Believe it or not, we'd actually recommend these over the $300 QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen), Bose's in-ear flagship. Why, you may ask? For starters, the QC Earbuds beat the QC Ultra for battery life; the former delivers up to 8.5 hours on a full charge, while the latter is limited to 6 hours. We also like the fact that the QC Earbuds have a dedicated 'Off' setting for ANC. With the Bose QC Ultra, you need to create a custom sound profile to turn ANC all the way down manually; there's no simple on/off toggle. We should also mention that the QC Earbuds are available in seven colors, whereas the QC Ultra is limited to five. The Bose QuietComfort Earbuds are the cheapest Bose in-ears on the market, but they lack spatial audio features It's a little hard to get excited about calling a $180 pair of earbuds "cheap," but Bose products often come at a premium price. So, what exactly are you giving up by not going with the more expensive QC Ultra (2nd Gen)? One suite of features you'll miss out on is Bose Immersive Audio – a dashboard of spatial audio settings and customizations available for free in the Bose app. While the QC Earbuds do include Quiet and Aware presets (also in the Bose app), the multi-dimensional soundstage and head-tracking tech of Bose Immersive Audio isn't an option. The Bose QC Ultra also supports Bose CustomTune, another in-app feature that calibrates audio and ANC in real time to deliver the best sound quality and noise isolation for your ear shape. Side-by-side, the QC Ultra offers improved noise-canceling, too, but probably not enough difference in attenuation to warrant spending another $120. Oddly enough, there was also a second generation of the Bose QC Earbuds, but they're not available to purchase brand-new (we're not exactly sure why). Bose headphones, the cheapest set of cans you can currently get your hands on is the , usually found for around the $250 mark.

articles.title: Republicans are flooding Senate races with ad money, but paying a premium
articles.desc: Republicans are pouring millions more into Senate TV ads, but Democrats are stretching their dollars further in several key battlegrounds.
articles.content: Republicans are flooding Senate races with ad money, but paying a premium | United States Pick countries on the world map and get breaking news alerts in your browser — free, no app. Republicans are pouring millions more into Senate TV ads, but Democrats are stretching their dollars further in several key battlegrounds. Republicans are spending hundreds of millions of dollars on advertising in battleground Senate races as they scramble to defend increasingly competitive GOP seats in the final stretch of the midterms. But when it comes to how far they can stretch a dollar, they’re effectively paying premium prices at Whole Foods while Democrats are shopping deals at Costco. RELATED STORY | Trump is heading all the way to Alaska in a sign of just how close its Senate race may be Across nine of the most competitive Senate races last month, Republicans cumulatively outspent Democrats on broadcast TV ads by nearly 100% more, $233 million to $121 million, according to AdImpact data, but only saw about 40% more rating points. The disparity comes down to a difference in strategy. Republicans are relying heavily on outside groups, like super PACs, that pay elevated rates for ads and are making big buys late in the campaign, when inventory is stretched. By contrast, Democrats are taking advantage of discounted rates for candidates and earlier, less expensive reservations. At this stage in the game, Republicans are spending more to get less, which means the “shock and awe” of their massive dollar advantage isn’t necessarily translating to an actual impact on the ground, according to veteran Republican strategist John Thomas. A better metric, he said, is to consider the gross rating points, or GRPs, a unit advertisers use to measure the reach and frequency of an ad campaign, independent of how much was paid for it. In those nine races – where outside groups accounted for about 9 in 10 Republican ad dollars, compared to about half for Democrats – Democrats paid $201 per GRP, while Republicans paid about $274. In some races in September, Democrats actually outpaced Republicans in GRPs, completely overcoming their spending edge. In North Carolina, for example, Republicans outspent Democrats by about $17 million to $14 million on TV ads in September, as former Gov. Roy Cooper poses a major threat to former RNC Chair Michael Whatley and the GOP chances of holding Sen. Thom Tillis’ seat. But Democrats got more than 71,000 GRPs from their spend while Republicans got about 58,000. And at the beginning of October – recognizing the costly, difficult road ahead for Whatley – Republicans actually began cutting their remaining ad bookings by about $15 million. Democrats were also outspent last month by Republicans in Maine by about 32%, another premier battleground race where former state Sen. Troy Jackson is looking to unseat veteran GOP incumbent Sen. Susan Collins, who has received major backing from national Republicans. But here, again, despite being outspent, Democrats got 6% more GRPs for their money. Even in Texas – where Democrats were blasted by Republican ad money in September, outspent more than 4 times over – the GRP gap was proportionally much smaller. Republicans got only 2.6 times more GRPs. A GOP super PAC had to spend more than $22 million to air its top ad, touting Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton’s record as a prosecutor, about 15,500 times in September. Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico’s campaign spent a little under $4 million to air its most aired ad, casting Paxton as “the most corrupt politician in Texas,” about 8,000 times. That amounts to less than one-fifth the spending for about half the airtime. Lauren French, communications director for Senate Majority PAC, a leading Democratic super PAC, also emphasized that buying TV late in the cycle becomes exorbitantly expensive. “The nitty-gritty of campaigning is that not all ad space costs the same,” she said. “If you are buying something in February, it’s going to be a

articles.desc: The supermarket giant made the announcement ahead of what it expects to be a busy Christmas
articles.content: Tesco issues '28,000 jobs' announcement ahead of Christmas | Bristol Live Tesco issues '28,000 jobs' announcement ahead of Christmas The supermarket giant made the announcement ahead of what it expects to be a busy Christmas This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Tesco has announced that it will hire 28,000 temporary staff to deal with the busy festive season. The supermarket says it wants to hear from anyone wishing for a job this Christmas. It adds that roles will 'mainly' involve working in Superstores and Extra stores either serving customers or picking items for home delivery. Shifts are said to be available right through the day, including early mornings and evenings, and applicants 'can find an opportunity that suits them'. Tesco's website says some roles are already open and more will continue to be added throughout October. The pay is said to be from £13.28 per hour (£14.55 inside the M25) and a night shift boost of £2.35. Tesco, which made the announcement on October 3, says there will be chances to move into permanent jobs after the festive season where positions come up. Ela Golab, Tesco Group's people services director, says the supermarket is looking for people who can offer 'warmth and enthusiasm' with no experience necessary. There is no need to have a CV to apply and anyone interested can find roles and apply at https://www.tesco.com/careers/en-GB/festive . Interviews are being held in person and are said to last 30 minutes. Ela Golab, Tesco Group's people services director, said: "We’re excited to be recruiting festive colleagues to help make this a season to remember for our customers. We're looking for people who can bring warmth, enthusiasm and a helpful service to every shopping trip. “We’re also keen to hear from applicants who may want to stay with us after Christmas and begin building a career at Tesco. No day is ever the same and festive colleagues will be able to feel the impact they make on every shift as they send customers home with a smile. What's more, no experience is necessary - just the right attitude." articles.title: L&T Inks MoU with TuTr Hyperloop for Next-Generation Mobility Infrastructure
articles.desc: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with TuTr Hyperloop Private Ltd, an IIT Madras-incubated deep-tech mobility start-up, to explore opportunities in the development and deployment of next-generation mobility technologies and infrastructure in India. The MoU establis
articles.content: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with TuTr Hyperloop Private Ltd, an IIT Madras-incubated deep-tech mobility start-up, to explore opportunities in the development and deployment of next-generation mobility technologies and infrastructure in India. The MoU establishes a framework for jointly exploring and pursuing opportunities in the emerging mobility ecosystem, with project-specific engagements to be undertaken through separate agreements. The collaboration combines L&T's engineering, procurement and construction expertise with TuTr Hyperloop's capabilities in indigenous electromagnetic propulsion and advanced mobility systems. The two organisations will assess opportunities across a range of infrastructure and technology domains, including Linear Induction Motor-based propulsion systems, vacuum tube infrastructure, pressure management systems, civil and structural works, electrical infrastructure, signalling, telecommunications and systems integration. The partnership envisages a complementary division of responsibilities spanning technology development, engineering, procurement, manufacturing, construction, installation and testing, as required for individual projects. The organisations will also engage with prospective customers to evaluate technical feasibility, commercial viability and implementation requirements. By bringing together indigenous deep-tech innovation and large-scale infrastructure execution capabilities, the collaboration seeks to support the development of future-ready transportation systems in India. It will also explore opportunities across freight and logistics, port connectivity, industrial transportation and other emerging mobility applications. For TuTr Hyperloop, the collaboration aligns with its broader vision of developing modular, indigenous mobility technologies, beginning with Linear Induction Motor-based systems and progressively advancing towards magnetic levitation and vacuum-based transportation applications. Commenting on the collaboration, Mr S V Desai, Whole-Time Director, Senior Executive Vice President – Infrastructure, L&T, said: “Hyperloop represents an exciting frontier in next-generation mobility, with the potential to redefine the movement of people and goods. Its innovative propulsion technology and low-friction environment enable faster transit, improved logistics efficiency, reduced energy consumption and lower emissions. Translating such technological innovation into practical deployment requires robust engineering, scalable infrastructure and close collaboration across the ecosystem. Our partnership with TuTr Hyperloop is a step in that direction”. Prof. Satya Chakravarthy, Professor, IIT Madras, said: “The transition of advanced mobility technologies from research and development to real-world deployment requires strong collaboration between academia, technology developers and industry. This partnership between TuTr Hyperloop and L&T brings together complementary strengths that can help address the engineering and infrastructure challenges involved in scaling next-generation transportation systems. It is an encouraging step towards translating indigenous innovation into practical, deployable solutions for India”. Dr Aravind S Bharadwaj, Co-Founder and CEO, TuTr Hyperloop, said: “At TuTr Hyperloop, our focus is on developing indigenous mobility technologies that can address real-world transportation and logistics challenges. A series on how Asia’s people of faith are responding to climate changes and disasters. Mobile app launched for World Youth Day 2027 pilgrims The platform will be updated before and during the event A screegrab of the WYD 2027 app available on Google Play. The organizing committee for World Youth Day 2027 Seoul has launched a mobile application to help pilgrims prepare for and navigate the global Catholic youth gathering. The provisional ‘WYD 2027’ App brings together practical travel information, spiritual resources, event schedules, maps, and details about Catholic pilgrimage sites in the South Korean capital, organizers said. The app is available on the Apple App Store and Google Play in Korean and English. Spanish, French, Portuguese, and Italian versions are planned. World Youth Day Seoul is scheduled for Aug. 3-8, 2027, and will be the second edition of the international Catholic youth gathering held in Asia after Manila hosted it in 1995. The home screen displays a countdown to the main event and provides direct access to preparation materials, the official prayer, the theme scripture, key schedules, and Catholic pilgrimage sites in Seoul. A preparation section offers advice on travel kits, spiritual preparation, pilgrim packages, and basic Korean expressions for greetings, directions, and use in churches and during Mass. It also contains guidance on South Korea’s summer weather, voltage and plug types, packing, public behavior, local regulations and emergency alerts. The app’s map currently lists 24 locations, including Catholic holy sites, museums and event venues, and is intended to help users plan routes and transportation in Seoul. A museum pilgrimage program allows registered users to verify visits to three sites — the History Museum at Myeongdong Cathedral, the Seosomun Shrine History Museum and the Korean Catholic Martyrs’ Museum at Jeoldusan — and receive a completion certificate. The app also provides information about the Korean Catholic Church, its martyrs, local culture, public transportation and emergency procedures. articles.title: No Metro train trips were cut on Oct 10 despite station restrictions: DMRC to SC
articles.desc: New Delhi, Oct 14 (IANS) The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has told the Supreme Court that there was no reduction in the number of Metro train trips on October 10, despite restrictions on entry and exit at several stations ahead of a proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) G
articles.content: New Delhi, Oct 14 (IANS) The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has told the Supreme Court that there was no reduction in the number of Metro train trips on October 10, despite restrictions on entry and exit at several stations ahead of a proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. In a compliance affidavit filed before the apex court, the DMRC said 271 trains were inducted into service, and all 4,157 scheduled train trips were operated across the network on October 10, maintaining the standard Saturday schedule. The affidavit, filed by DMRC General Manager (Legal) Group Captain Sanjay Vinayakrao Kute (Retd.), was submitted in compliance with the Supreme Court's October 9 order directing the DMRC, railway authorities and Delhi Police (Traffic) to file compliance reports on the operation of public transport services in the national capital. The DMRC said the Delhi Police had initially directed the closure of entry and exit gates at 57 stations out of the total 303 stations in the Delhi-NCR Metro network. However, following the Supreme Court's intervention, the number of affected stations was reduced to 45 through a modified communication issued on October 9. Custom Ad: Multiplex "The entire Metro network comprises 303 stations. The notification dated 08.10.2026, which appears to have been placed before this Hon'ble Court, did not impose a complete ban on public transportation. It merely directed the closure of 57 out of the 303 stations for entry and exit purposes," the compliance report stated. The DMRC said restrictions on entry and exit were confined to 45 stations, accounting for around 15 per cent of the network, while the remaining 258 stations, or over 85 per cent, continued to remain operational and accessible to commuters. It further said that 14 key interchange stations among those affected, including Rajiv Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Central Secretariat, Mandi House, Hauz Khas, Dilli Haat-INA and Netaji Subhash Place, continued to provide uninterrupted line-interchange facilities. The affidavit stated that commuters were able to change Metro corridors without disruption and that alternative stations remained open to minimise inconvenience to passengers. The affidavit said the entry and exit restrictions at all 45 stations were lifted from 10 p.m. on October 10 after the DMRC received directions from the Delhi Police to reopen them. However, it added that the police authorities issued fresh communications on October 12 directing the closure of entry and exit facilities at six Metro stations between 6 a.m. and 4 p.m. The closure period was subsequently extended until 5 p.m. on the same day. On the functioning of stations such as GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya, the DMRC said there was no complete prohibition on passenger movement and that arrangements had been made to facilitate the exit of commuters arriving by train. It said the exit gates at Vishwavidyalaya Metro Station remained operational, while passenger movement at GTB Nagar was regulated by personnel deployed on the ground, with Gate No. 3 kept open to facilitate passengers leaving the station. The DMRC also detailed the steps taken to disseminate information about the restrictions, including regular updates on its official social media handles, announcements through the Operations Control Centre and train operators, advisory signages at station gates, and updates on its website and the DMRC Sarthi app. It said additional staff and ground marshals were deployed at major interchange stations to guide commuters, manage passenger flows and minimise inconvenience. The network was monitored in real time in coordination with police authorities. The affidavit further disclosed that approximately 32 lakh passengers travelled on the Metro network on October 10, against around 58 lakh passengers on a normal second Saturday. The DMRC said the lower ridership could be attributed to the proposed protest, which appeared to have prompted many commuters to avoid travelling and refrain from their usual daily activities, including attending work or conducting business. The affidavit said the DMRC would continue to act in accordance with security assessments and directions issued by law enforcement agencies while ensuring the smooth functioning of the Metro network, subject to requirements for maintaining law and order. The development comes amid contempt petitions alleging wilful disobedience of the Supreme Court's October 9 directions concerning restrictions on Metro and railway services ahead of the proposed protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. On October 9, a Bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant observed that the restrictions appeared to be "overreaching" and clarified that there should be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains. The apex court had directed the authorities to permit Metro and other railway services to operate in a suitably regulated manner, in accordance with the principle of proportionality, and to issue traffic advisories to prevent inconvenience to commuters. On October 11, a Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, hearing a clutch of contempt petitions alleging wilful disobedience of the earlier order, directed that Metro and railway services should function normally unless restrictions became necessary due to a disturbance to public order. The Supreme Court also sought details of the affected Metro stations and directed the authorities to file compliance reports explaining their adherence to the earlier directions. The proposed protest had prompted the Delhi Police to impose restrictions in parts of the national capital, citing concerns over public safety, traffic management and law and order. --IANS pds/uk

articles.title: Around 400 BCE, People Across Northern Iberia Abandoned Their Fortified Settlements. The Real Story Is What Came Next
articles.desc: Around 400 BCE, people across northern Iberia left their fortified settlements and built new ones. A new study looks at how that move really unfolded, and the timeline is not what you might expect.
articles.content: Around 400 BCE, People Across Northern Iberia Abandoned Their Fortified Settlements. The Real Story Is What Came Next Around 400 BCE, communities across northern Iberia abandoned their and founded new ones. A new radiocarbon study finds that the two halves of this shift moved at very different speeds: the old sites emptied quickly, while the new ones spread slowly. Climate shifts, migration and conflict have all been blamed, though nobody has settled on a cause, and the changes looked different from one place to the next. Northern Iberia works well as a test case, given its many kinds of settlements and plenty of radiocarbon dates. of INCIPIT-CSIC used that record to build a timeline. He drew on in five areas: the Atlantic region, the western and eastern Cantabrian regions, and the western and eastern Northern Plateau. Bayesian models and other statistical tests let him compare when sites were abandoned with when new ones began. The decline started in the western Cantabrian region, where the first sites were left behind . From there, the trend moved to the Atlantic region and the western Northern Plateau. By the last decades of the fifth century BCE, people had abandoned sites at both the western and eastern edges of the study area. Most Early Iron Age settlements stood empty in under a hundred years. According to , no single date marks the break. Each region went through its own sharp change over a few decades, and the older and newer phases In a few places, people did come back to abandoned sites later on. Rebuilding ran at a slower pace. New settlements began to appear , first in the western Cantabrian and Atlantic regions. Larger settlements followed, and many had and sat closer to good farmland. They spread over a much longer stretch of time and moved across the Northern Plateau. In the far east, fortified settlements became common only around the start of . In the article’s own summary, the old settlements emptied within a few decades, while the new ones The shift also left smaller marks in the ground. Short-term camps, and burials show up in the record, mostly in the Atlantic region, and their dates overlap with the fading of the older settlements. Other parts of the Cantabrian coast have too little evidence to tell whether the same thing happened there. People did more than change addresses. Late Iron Age settlements were bigger and more complex, and some regions saw wider gaps between rich and poor. This new pattern lasted until Roman times. links the changes to a broad reorganization of communities, while pointing out that the pace and form differed from region to region. The study does not say why people left. War, population growth and shifting social structures are all on the table, and the early decline of hillforts in Asturias is still a puzzle. What the work gives researchers is a firm timeline for each stage, so they can test possible causes against solid dates. The paper also offers a method others could reuse, combining with estimates of how much date ranges overlap. This shows whether events happened together, one after another, or at separate times in different regions.
